newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan generals and ex-rebels preach peace.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan generals and ex-rebels preach peace.

text.p: Two army generals and a rebel commander, once bitter enemies in Guatemala's 36-year guerrilla conflict, travelled together to a remote jungle village on Monday to tell villagers the war was over.

"Our presence here is a good example of tolerance and reconciliation. We have been able to leave weapons behind and to give each other a fraternal hug," said Defence Minister Gen. Julio Balconi, addressing about 2,000 villagers in Cantabal.

The symbolic visit to Cantabal came a day after Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) rebels signed a historic peace treaty to end the war which left an estimated 140,000 dead.

Balconi, Gen. Otto Perez of the government's peace negotiating team, and URNG commander Rolando Moran met with cheering villagers in the central plaza of Cantabal in the battle-scarred jungles of Ixcan in northern Guatemala.
The crowd chanted "Long live the URNG," and "Long live the army," apparently signalling their readiness to bury the hatchet.
The mostly Indian people of the Ixcan region suffered some of the worst atrocities committed by the Guatemalan army at the height of counter-insurgency campaigns in the 1980s.

Just miles away from Cantabal, in the town of Cuarto Pueblo, 325 people died in a 1982 massacre in which soldiers dismembered peasants, burned down churches full of people and swung babies against trees until they were dead.

Travelling with the men-of-war turned peacemakers was Indian peasant leader Rigoberta Menchu, who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992. "We decided to come to see whether the people of this town are ready to begin reconciliation," Menchu said in a speech.

In Cantabal, former combatants of the URNG, left-wing exiles returning from Mexico, and paramilitary "Civilian Self-Defence Patrols" which carried out army espionage, will have to learn to live side by side for peace to work.
To illustrate the need for reconciliation, Menchu, Moran and General Perez hugged other after planting a tree for peace in the centre of Cantabal.
